title: Prisco's NFL Week 12 Power Rankings: Thanksgiving Games Test Contenders’ Championship Hopes
body:
The NFL’s Week 12 slate has turned the Thanksgiving holiday into a high‑stakes proving ground for the league’s emerging contenders, and veteran analyst Pete Prisco has released his latest power‑ranking list to reflect the shifting landscape. With the Detroit Lions, Dallas Cowboys, and Buffalo Bills each eyeing playoff berths, the traditional turkey‑day matchups have become a litmus test for teams hoping to cement their status among the season’s elite. Prisco’s rankings place the Lions at the top of the pack, rewarding their dominant defensive performance and a potent offense that finally clicked, while the Cowboys and Bills settle into the middle, each grappling with inconsistency that could determine whether they remain in the postseason conversation.

Prisco’s assessment begins with Detroit, a team that has transformed its early‑season woes into a relentless march toward the NFC North crown. The Lions’ defense, anchored by a ferocious pass rush and a secondary that finally stopped giving up big plays, has forced a league‑high number of turnovers in the past three weeks. Coupled with a balanced attack that blends a revitalized running game with an efficient passing attack, the Lions have shown the consistency that eluded them last year. Their Week 12 victory over the New York Giants, a game that featured a 30‑point surge in the second half, solidified their claim as the most improved squad and earned them the top spot in Prisco’s hierarchy.

The Dallas Cowboys, perennial Thanksgiving hosts, sit at No. 3 in the rankings, reflecting a season of highs and lows that has left them teetering on the edge of the NFC East race. While the Cowboys’ offense remains one of the most explosive units in the league—thanks largely to a dynamic quarterback‑receiver duo and a revitalized offensive line—their defense has struggled to contain opposing rushers, yielding an average of 140 rushing yards per game. The Week 12 showdown against the Philadelphia Eagles highlighted these vulnerabilities, as Dallas surrendered a late‑game comeback that ultimately cost them a win. Prisco notes that the Cowboys must tighten up their defensive schemes if they hope to remain viable playoff contenders beyond the holiday weekend.

Buffalo, perched at No. 5, illustrates the volatility that has defined the AFC East this season. The Bills entered the Thanksgiving stretch with a 7‑4 record, but a narrow loss to the Miami Dolphins exposed lingering issues in their secondary and a lack of depth at the linebacker position. Despite quarterback Josh Allen’s continued excellence—averaging 285 passing yards per game—Buffalo’s inability to close out tight contests could prove costly. Prisco emphasizes that the Bills’ fate now hinges on their performance against the New England Patriots in Week 13; a win could propel them back into the top tier, while another stumble might relegate them to a peripheral role in the playoff picture.

Other notable movements in the rankings include the Seattle Seahawks, who climbed to No. 7 after a dominant win over the Los Angeles Rams that showcased a resurging run game and a defense capable of generating pressure without excessive blitzing. Conversely, the New England Patriots slipped to No. 10 following a series of offensive miscues that have left them scrambling for consistency. Prisco also highlighted the rising importance of special teams play, noting that teams like the Indianapolis Colts have leveraged superior return units to swing momentum in close games—a factor that could become decisive as the regular season winds down.

Looking ahead, the Thanksgiving games serve as a micro‑cosm of the broader narratives shaping the 2026 NFL season. Teams that can capitalize on the heightened visibility and pressure of the holiday weekend stand to gain not only a coveted win but also a psychological edge over rivals. As the league approaches the final stretch, the power rankings will likely continue to fluctuate, with each Thursday night offering a chance for underdogs to upset the established order. For fans and analysts alike, the real story will be how these mid‑season performances translate into postseason positioning, setting the stage for an electrifying run‑in to the playoffs.
